title: Separated locally quasi-finite algebraic spaces over schemes are schemes
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $T$ be a scheme over $S$, let $E$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $f:E\to T$ be a morphism. Assume that $f$ is locally quasi-finite in the chartwise sense: for every representable etale morphism $V\to E$ with $V$ a scheme, the composite $V\to T$ is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Assume also that the diagonal $E\to E\times_T E$ is a closed immersion after every scheme base change [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then there exist a scheme $Z$ over $T$ and an isomorphism of algebraic spaces over $T$ between $h_Z$ and $E$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-separated-lqf-affine-relation-cover] to $f:E\to T$. Its hypotheses are exactly the two assumptions of the item. Obtain an open covering $(X_i)$ over affine opens $T_i$ with affine atlases $U_i$, affine closed kernel relations $R_i$, and quotient identifications $U_i/R_i\simeq X_i$. Each $X_i/T_i$ retains chartwise local quasi-finiteness and testwise closed diagonal, and the quotient identifications persist after scheme base change.

For each $i$ and $u\in U_i$, apply [lem-a1-closed-relation-schematic-neighbourhood] to $X_i/T_i$ and its presentation. All its hypotheses were supplied in step 1. It gives an open subspace $W_{i,u}\subseteq X_i$ represented by a scheme and containing the image of $u$. Surjectivity of the atlas implies these opens cover $|X_i|$. For a scheme section $h_H\to X_i$, their pullbacks are open subschemes covering $H$: each field-valued point of $H$ maps into some $W_{i,u}$ and thus factors through its pullback.

source.place: Tag 03XX, fourth and final proof paragraphs.

proof.text: Each $X_i$ is a Zariski sheaf because it is an fppf sheaf [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The representable open subfunctors of step 2 satisfy all clauses of [lem-pc-schemes-criterion], so $X_i$ is represented by a scheme. The covering of step 1 has representable open inclusions and covers on every scheme section. The same criterion, now for the Zariski sheaf $E$, gives an isomorphism $e:h_Z\simeq E$ for an $S$-scheme $Z$.

source.place: Tag 03XX, local-to-global reductions and final sentence; Schemes Tag 01JJ.

proof.text: For $\alpha=f\circ e:h_Z\to h_T$, put $g=\alpha_Z(\mathrm{id}_Z):Z\to T$. Naturality gives $\alpha_H(a)=g\circ a$ for every $S$-scheme $H$ and $a:H\to Z$. Thus $e$ is an isomorphism over $T$ and $Z$ with structure map $g$ has the required property.

source.place: Tag 03XX, conclusion; Yoneda naturality written out.
